sweep_summary: Konzo (konz1239) is not in the catalog; It places Konzo with Nande in Group I: distinctive prosodemes (H*B accentual melody, four Proto-Bantu tone classes preserved, pp. 405-406), no surface length contrast, and a penultimate syllable with 'culmination de longueur, mais non de hauteur' (p. 483) / 'culmination d'intensité et de longueur' (Annexe p. 497) — lexical tone plus non-tonal penultimate prominence, not demarcative stress. Konzo data are second-hand (Tucker 1960 only; 'les informations sont fragmentaires', fn. p. 205). Bastin 2003 p. 504 (on file) corroborates: in Nande-Konzo length is limited to the utterance-final penultimate vowel. high priority as the first-hand source), Tucker & Bryan 1957 'Characteristics of Konzo' (DOI 10.4324/9781315105703-3, T&F 403), Kambale n.d. grammar sketch (host parked, Wayback offline). All three quoted passages are present verbatim at the stated locators (page numbers = running page numbers in the DDL PDF): (1) p. 483, sec. 3.5.2 'La typologie', item (c): 'langues a culmination de longueur, mais non de hauteur, sur la penultieme (langues a prosodemes distinctifs, mais sans opposition de longueur1) : nande et konzo; langi; nyanja et chewa; makonde2; shambaa, bondei, zigula, ngulu; mwani, comorien, pokomo, mijikenda; asu; da[esh]ida et saghala; chaga;' -- exact match, including footnote 1 ('langues sans opposition de longueur realisee... opposition de longueur sous-jacente qui interfere a…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Konzo (grouped with Nande) is a language with lexically distinctive tone (an H vs. Ø 'accentual' system realizing an H*L melody) and no surface vowel-length contrast; independently of tone, the penultimate syllable carries a culminative prominence realized as extra length and intensity (penultimate lengthening/stress), while pitch does not culminate on the penult (an H does not migrate to an unmarked penult).
new_statements.exceptions: Philippson flags (fn. p. 205) that his Konzo information (from Tucker 1960) is fragmentary and the Annexe profile is headed 'Nande/(Konzo)', i.e. primarily Nande with Konzo assumed parallel; p. 483 fn. 1 notes these languages lack a realized length contrast although some have been analysed with underlying length interacting with tone; item 9 p. 497: a post-lexical H on an unassociated word-final syllable 'se déplace sur la pénultième devant pause' in certain syntactic contexts.
new_statements.domain_note: Penultimate prominence is culminative length (+ intensity), not pitch. Bastin 2003:504 (independent handbook source, on file) locates Nande-Konzo length on 'the penultimate vowel at the end of an utterance or elicitation forms', i.e. the domain is the utterance/pre-pausal word (citation forms), consistent with Kinande intonational-phrase penultimate lengthening (Hyman 2019, table 30). Statement is second-hand for Konzo: Philippson's Konzo data come from Tucker 1960 (and Tucker & Bryan 1957).
new_statements.identity_note: Philippson's appendix profile is headed 'Nande/(Konzo)': it is primarily a Nande (Kinande, nand1264, JD42, DR Congo) profile with Konzo (konz1239, JD41, Uganda/DRC) bracketed as an extremely close variety; the p. 483 typology names 'konzo' explicitly, and his Konzo data come from Tucker 1960 / Tucker & Bryan 1957 (Konzo of the Ruwenzori, Uganda side). Bastin 2003 likewise treats 'Nande-Konzo' as one unit. The other open items read (Hyman 2019, Kenstowicz 2008, Black 1995, Jones 2014) describe Kinande only. Beware the unrelated Austronesian 'Konjo' (Coastal/Highland Konjo, kjc/kjk, Sulawesi) that dominates search results.

new_statements.reading: Konzo is a tone/pitch-accent language (H*B melody on a lexically marked syllable, Proto-Bantu tone classes retained) without a surface vowel-length contrast, in which the penultimate syllable carries a fixed prominence realised as lengthening and intensity but not as pitch — i.e. lexical tone plus a non-tonal penultimate stress-like prominence (penultimate lengthening), not a demarcative penultimate stress of the Swahili type. Caveats: the Konzo evidence is second-hand (Tucker 1960), Philippson brackets Konzo with Nande and calls the Konzo information 'fragmentaires' (fn. p. 205); Bastin 2003 p. 504 independently confirms length limited to the utterance-final penultimate in Nande-Konzo.

Annexe p. 497, Groupe I 'Nande/(Konzo)': no surface length contrast; 'système accentuel à mélodie H*B' (restricted tone system); item 10 status of the penultimate = 'culmination d'intensité et de longueur'.
